capture_policy: Exact short excerpts with URLs, re-access interval and locations; no full copyrighted source copied into the manuscript. Earlier same-essay source artifacts were not read.

sources.title: Adaptive abilities

access.method: web.run primary-source open/find; short excerpts re-accessed in the recorded interval

sources.read_extent: Entire main text §§1–6 and endnotes 1–11; relevant bibliography entries. Publisher HTML.
sources.locations_used: §2, especially bundle organization; §4, two dimensions of adaptivity; §5, first-order and meta-powers, especially paragraphs at retrieval lines 218–229; §6, possession/exercise distinction.
sources.supports: Established integration requirement, distinction between how and whether/when, and implementation left open.
sources.limitations: Does not independently settle attribution of an unknown helper's monitoring; no claim that this source endorses the revised attribution proposal. No priority certificate.

sources.title: They've Lost Control: Reflections on Skill

access.method: web.run primary-source open/find; short excerpts re-accessed in the recorded interval

sources.read_extent: Author-hosted personal-copy PDF: abstract plus §4 including §§4.1–4.3 and §5 conclusion; not the entire article.
sources.locations_used: §4.1–§4.3, PDF pages 18–23 (one-based); §4.2 excerpt on PDF page 20, retrieval line 783.
sources.supports: Strategic, attentional, and motor control can be distinguished; attention may be automatically deployed and responsive to goals.
sources.limitations: Empirical studies cited within Fridland were not independently audited. No claim about her answer to the hidden-helper case.

sources.title: The Extended Mind

access.method: web.run primary-source open/find; short excerpts re-accessed in the recorded interval

sources.read_extent: Author-hosted HTML §§4–5, plus selected preceding passages about reliable coupling. Publisher bibliographic metadata appeared in the primary publisher search result.
sources.locations_used: §4 notebook discussion; §5, retrieval lines 117–124, including social cases at line 123.
sources.supports: The cited discussion concerns extended standing belief, including stable availability/use and social trust/reliance/accessibility.
sources.limitations: No inference that their listed features are jointly necessary in every case. Author HTML has an inconsistent pagination note; bibliography follows publisher metadata.

sources.title: Stubborn cases: a precautionist account of negligence

access.method: web.run primary-source open/find; short excerpts re-accessed in the recorded interval

sources.read_extent: Publisher abstract; §§4.1–4.2; substantial selected passages of §4.3 and conclusion. Not a full audit of the paper or its cases.
sources.locations_used: §4.1, retrieval lines 158–173, especially the duty formulation at line 169.
sources.supports: Precautionist duties concern maintaining conditions that make existing knowledge available for action.
sources.limitations: Used only to distinguish precautionary demands from supported present guidance. The source's negligence judgments and general normative theory are not endorsed or independently established.

source_scope_limit: Selected primary-source verification for this single revision, not a systematic literature search.
